description: We are a team of Computer Science students passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. Our interests include software development, AI, web technologies, and creative problem-solving. We aim to combine our technical and creative skills to build practical solutions for challenges related to space and Earth. We welcome teammates with skills in programming, data science, research, UI/UX, and scientific problem-solving.
summary:
FLARE AI (Fire and Life-safety Analysis and Research Engine) is a student-built web application that helps users explore microgravity combustion research for future space habitats. We developed a React frontend and FastAPI backend with a curated, provenance-preserving catalog of NASA-linked Physical Sciences Informatics investigations, source-indexed evidence retrieval, scenario analysis, comparison tools, and cited research briefs.

Users can enter hypothetical mission conditions , such as oxygen concentration, pressure, environment, and research objectiveand receive transparent research-relevance rankings. The system shows supporting sources, evidence excerpts, data gaps, and limitations instead of filling unknown values with assumptions. An optional AI assistant synthesizes retrieved evidence, while a local seeded dataset provides an evidence-only fallback if an external model or network service fails.

FLARE AI addresses the challenge of making complex space-combustion research easier to discover and interpret. It is important because future habitat planning depends on understanding available evidence and its limitations. The system communicates research relevance, not fire risk or safety certification, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
details:
What the project does

FLARE AI (Fire and Life-safety Analysis and Research Engine) is a student-built web application for exploring microgravity combustion research relevant to future space habitats. It provides:

  • A searchable catalog of curated, source-backed investigations.
  • Provenance details for each source, including document identity, URL, verification status, and available page or section information.
  • Hypothetical mission scenario analysis using inputs such as environment, oxygen concentration, pressure, material, and research objective.
  • Research-relevance rankings with transparent score components and limitations.
  • Investigation comparison, evidence retrieval, cited research briefs, and an optional AI research assistant.
  • A local seeded dataset that allows the demo to continue working when an external LLM or network service is unavailable.

The system does not estimate fire risk, certify safety, or treat microgravity results as proven lunar or Martian performance.

Benefits and intended impact

FLARE AI makes technical research easier to discover and interpret. It helps users quickly identify which investigations may be relevant to a question, inspect the evidence behind a result, and understand what information is missing. The system is designed to reduce unsupported assumptions by preserving unknown values, attaching citations to evidence, and separating source-reported facts from generated interpretation.

Its intended impact is to support better research planning for space-habitat combustion studies, education, and early mission-concept discussions. It is a research support tool, not a replacement for engineering analysis, experiment design, or safety certification.

Tools and technologies

We used:

  • Frontend: React and TypeScript.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data storage: SQLite.
  • Validation and schemas: Pydantic models and a generated OpenAPI contract.
  • Evidence processing: Local PDF and metadata extraction with provenance and SHA-256 verification.
  • Search and retrieval: Deterministic local text indexing and evidence ranking.
  • Optional AI: An OpenAI-compatible chat provider with request timeouts and evidence-only fallback behavior.
  • Testing: Pytest, FastAPI test clients, Playwright, and Chromium.
  • Deployment: Vite production builds, Docker, and environment-variable configuration.
  • Hardware: No specialized hardware was required; development used standard computers and browser-based software.

Creative aspects

The project combines scientific data handling, transparent relevance scoring, source-aware retrieval, and conversational interaction in one workflow. Instead of presenting a single opaque AI answer, FLARE AI shows the investigation match, score breakdown, retrieved excerpts, citations, research gaps, and limitations together. The offline fallback also makes the demo resilient and repeatable.

Factors considered

The team considered scientific provenance, missing data, source availability, uncertainty, partial-gravity limitations, privacy of user inputs, external-service failure, request limits, deployment security, and clear communication for non-specialist users. We also ensured the project is described as student-built and not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
